title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 119 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 587–590 (Night 119, continuing directly from nights-118), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 119 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. ʿAzīz goes on with his tale to Tāj al-Mulūk. As he leaves, the lady gives him the cloth with the gazelle on it, her sister Nūr al-Hudā’s work, and in his joy he forgets the line of verse his cousin ʿAzīza gave him. ʿAzīza, weeping, makes him carry her verses to the lady night after night, and the lady answers each in verse; but ʿAzīza is wasting away and fainting, and her last lines are a farewell. When ʿAzīz recites them, the lady cries out that the woman who made them is dead, curses him for her death, and sends him home, where he finds ʿAzīza lying dead behind the door and his mother laying her blood on his neck. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the nineteenth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and nineteenth night,
sentences.n: al-tāsiʿata ʿashara, “nineteenth”: as in the nights before, the print has the masculine عشر beside the feminine night, and it is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الشَّابَّ قَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَلَمَّا أَرَدْتُ الِانْصِرَافَ أَمْسَكَتْنِي وَقَالَتْ قِفْ حَتَّى أُخْبِرَكَ بِشَيْءٍ وَأُوصِيَكَ وَصِيَّةً
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba qāla li-tāji al-mulūki fa-lammā aradtu al-inṣirāfa amsakatnī wa-qālat qif ḥattā ukhbiraka bi-shayʾin wa-ūṣiyaka waṣiyyatan
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the youth said to Tāj al-Mulūk: And when I wanted the departing, she held me fast and said: Stay, until I inform you of a thing and charge you (with) a charge.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man said to Tāj al-Mulūk: When I wanted to leave, she held me back and said, “Wait, so that I can tell you something and give you a charge.”
sentences.n: The night opens by going back over the last lines of the night before. The print runs السعيد and ان together as one word. ūṣiyaka waṣiyyatan: a verb with its own noun as object, “charge you a charge”, a common Arabic way of giving weight to the act.

sentences.t: فَوَقَفْتُ فَحَلَّتْ مِنْدِيلًا وَأَخْرَجَتْ هَذِهِ الْخِرْقَةَ وَنَشَرَتْهَا قُدَّامِي فَوَجَدْتُ فِيهَا صُورَةَ غَزَالٍ عَلَى هَذَا الْمِثَالِ فَتَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْهَا غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ فَأَخَذْتُهُ وَتَوَاعَدْتُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاهَا أَنِّي آتِي إِلَيْهَا كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ فِي ذَلِكَ الْبُسْتَانِ ثُمَّ انْصَرَفْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا وَأَنَا فَرْحَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaftu fa-ḥallat mindīlan wa-akhrajat hādhihi al-khirqata wa-nasharathā quddāmī fa-wajadtu fīhā ṣūrata ghazālin ʿalā hādhā al-mithāli fa-taʿajjabtu minhā ghāyata al-ʿajabi fa-akhadhtuhu wa-tawāʿadtu anā wa-iyyāhā annī ātī ilayhā kulla laylatin fī dhālika al-bustāni thumma inṣaraftu min ʿindihā wa-anā farḥānu
sentences.l: And I stayed, and she untied a kerchief and brought-out this rag and spread it before me; and I found in it the picture of a gazelle upon this pattern, and I marvelled at it the utmost of marvelling. And I took it, and I made-a-promise, I and she, that I would come to her every night in that garden; then I departed from her presence, and I (was) glad.
sentences.i: So I waited, and she untied a kerchief, took out this piece of cloth and spread it in front of me, and I found on it the figure of a gazelle, worked just like this; I wondered at it beyond measure. I took it, and she and I agreed that I would come to her every night in that garden. Then I left her, full of joy.
sentences.n: hādhihi al-khirqa, “this piece of cloth”, ʿalā hādhā al-mithāl, “just like this”: ʿAzīz is holding the cloth as he speaks; it is the gazelle cloth Tāj al-Mulūk saw him weeping over. fa-akhadhtuhu, “I took it”: the masculine pronoun, though khirqa is feminine; it may mean the picture, or simply “the thing”.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ فَرَحِي نَسِيتُ الشِّعْرَ الَّذِي أَوْصَتْنِي بِهِ بِنْتُ عَمِّي وَحِينَ أَعْطَتْنِي الْخِرْقَةَ اللَّتِي فِيهَا صُورَةُ الْغَزَالِ قَالَتْ لِي هَذَا عَمَلُ أُخْتِي فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَمَااسْمُ أُخْتِكِ قَالَتِ اسْمُهَا نُورُالْهُدَى فَاحْتَفِظْ بِهَذِهِ الْخِرْقَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-min faraḥī nasītu al-shiʿra alladhī awṣatnī bihi bintu ʿammī wa-ḥīna aʿṭatnī al-khirqata allatī fīhā ṣūratu al-ghazāli qālat lī hādhā ʿamalu ukhtī fa-qultu lahā wa-mā ismu ukhtiki qālati ismuhā nūru al-hudā fa-iḥtafiẓ bi-hādhihi al-khirqati
sentences.l: And from my joy I forgot the verse which the daughter of my uncle had charged me with. And when she gave me the rag in which (was) the picture of the gazelle, she said to me: This (is) the work of my sister. And I said to her: And what (is) the name of your sister? She said: Her name (is) Nūr al-Hudā; so keep-safe this rag.
sentences.i: And in my joy I forgot the verse my cousin had charged me to recite. When she gave me the cloth with the gazelle on it, she said, “This is my sister’s work.” “And what is your sister’s name?” I asked. “Her name is Nūr al-Hudā,” she said; “so take good care of this cloth.”
sentences.n: allatī: the print spells it اللتي, with two lāms, as it often does. The print runs ومااسم and نورالهدى together. Nūr al-Hudā: “Light of Right Guidance”. awṣā bi-: “charge someone with” — the verb takes bi- for the thing charged; so iḥtafaẓa bi-, “keep hold of”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَدَّعْتُهَا وَانْصَرَفْتُ وَأَنَا فَرْحَانُ وَمَشَيْتُ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى ابْنَةِ عَمِّي فَوَجَدْتُهَا رَاقِدَةً فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي قَامَتْ وَدُمُوعُهَا تَجْرِي ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيَّ وَبَاسَتْ صَدْرِي وَقَالَتْ هَلْ فَعَلْتَ مَا أَوْصَيْتُكَ بِهِ مِنْ إِنْشَادِ الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: thumma waddaʿtuhā wa-inṣaraftu wa-anā farḥānu wa-mashaytu ilā an dakhaltu ʿalā ibnati ʿammī fa-wajadtuhā rāqidatan fa-lammā raʾatnī qāmat wa-dumūʿuhā tajrī thumma aqbalat ʿalayya wa-bāsat ṣadrī wa-qālat hal faʿalta mā awṣaytuka bihi min inshādi al-bayti
sentences.l: Then I bade-farewell to her and departed, and I (was) glad; and I walked until I entered upon the daughter of my uncle, and I found her lying-down. And when she saw me she rose, and her tears running; then she came-forward to me and kissed my chest and said: Have you done what I charged you with, of the reciting of the verse?
sentences.i: Then I said goodbye to her and went away full of joy, and walked on till I came in to my cousin. I found her lying down; when she saw me she rose, her tears running, came to me, kissed my breast and said, “Did you do what I charged you to do, and recite the verse?”
sentences.n: bāsat: “kissed”, the spoken verb bāsa, yabūsu.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنِّي نَسِيتُهُ وَمَا أَشْغَلَنِي عَنْهُ إِلَّا صُورَةُ هَذَا الْغَزَالِ وَرَمَيْتُ الْخِرْقَةَ قُدَّامَهَا فَقَامَتْ وَقَعَدَتْ وَلَمْ تُطِقِ الصَّبْرَ وَأَفَاضَتْ دَمْعَ الْعَيْنِ وَأَنْشَدَتْ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā innī nasītuhu wa-mā ashghalanī ʿanhu illā ṣūratu hādhā al-ghazāli wa-ramaytu al-khirqata quddāmahā fa-qāmat wa-qaʿadat wa-lam tuṭiqi al-ṣabra wa-afāḍat damʿa al-ʿayni wa-anshadat hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: And I said to her: I forgot it, and nothing distracted me from it except the picture of this gazelle; and I threw the rag before her. And she rose and sat, and could not bear the patience, and poured-out the tear of the eye, and recited these two verses:
sentences.i: I told her, “I forgot it; nothing put it out of my mind but the figure of this gazelle,” and I threw the cloth down in front of her. She stood up and sat down again, past all patience, let her tears pour, and recited these two lines:
sentences.n: ashghalanī, “distracted me”: the print has the fourth form, where Classical usage prefers shaghalanī. qāmat wa-qaʿadat, “she stood and sat”: she could not keep still.

sentences.t:
يَا طَالِبًا لِلْفِرَاقِ مَهْلًا * وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ الْعِنَاقُ
مَهْلًا فَطَبْعُ الزَّمَانِ غَدْرٌ * وَاٰخِرُ الصُّحْبَةِ الْفِرَاقُ
sentences.tr:
yā ṭāliban li-al-firāqi mahlan * wa-lā yaghurrannaka al-ʿināqu
mahlan fa-ṭabʿu al-zamāni ghadrun * wa-ākhiru al-ṣuḥbati al-firāqu
sentences.l:
O seeker of the parting, gently! * And let not the embracing deceive you.
Gently! For the nature of time (is) treachery, * and the end of the companionship (is) the parting.
sentences.i:
You who go seeking to part, go slowly, * and do not let embraces lead you astray.
Go slowly: the nature of time is betrayal, * and all companionship ends in parting.
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed. وَاٰخِرُ: the print writes the long ā of ākhir with a small dagger alif. li-al-firāqi: li- marks what is sought, “seeking parting”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا قٰلَتْ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي هَبْ لِي هَذِهِ الْخِرْقَةَ فَوَهَبْتُهَا لَهَا فَأَخَذَتْهَا وَنَشَرَتْهَا وَرَأَتْ مَا فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā qālat yā bna ʿammī hab lī hādhihi al-khirqata fa-wahabtuhā lahā fa-akhadhathā wa-nasharathā wa-raʾat mā fīhā
sentences.l: And when she had finished from her verse, she said: O son of my uncle, give to me this rag. And I gave it to her, and she took it and spread it out and saw what (was) in it.
sentences.i: When she had finished her verses, she said, “Cousin, give me this cloth.” I gave it to her; she took it, spread it out and looked at what was on it.
sentences.n: qālat, “she said”: the print spells it قلت, without the alif, which would otherwise read “I said”; it is pointed with a small dagger alif, and the sense (ʿAzīza is speaking, and he gives the cloth “to her”) leaves no doubt. yā bna ʿammī: the alif of ibn drops after yā, as the print writes it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاءَ وَقْتُ ذَهَابِي قَالَتْ لِي بِنْتُ عَمِّي اذْهَبْ مَصْحُوبًا بِالسَّلَامَةِ فَإِذَا انْصَرَفْتَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا فَأَنْشِدْهَا الْبَيْتَ الشِّعْرَ الَّذِي أَخْبَرْتُكَ بِهِ أَوَّلًا وَنَسِيتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾa waqtu dhahābī qālat lī bintu ʿammī idhhab maṣḥūban bi-al-salāmati fa-idhā inṣarafta min ʿindihā fa-anshidhā al-bayta al-shiʿra alladhī akhbartuka bihi awwalan wa-nasītahu
sentences.l: And when the time of my going came, the daughter of my uncle said to me: Go, accompanied by the safety; and when you depart from her presence, recite to her the verse, the poetry, which I told you of at first and you forgot it.
sentences.i: When the time came for me to go, my cousin said to me, “Go, and safety go with you; and when you leave her, recite to her the verse I told you of the first time, the one you forgot.”
sentences.n: maṣḥūban bi-al-salāma, “accompanied by safety”: a parting blessing; bi- names the companion. al-bayta al-shiʿra, “the verse, the poetry”: the print sets the two words side by side, where Classical Arabic would say bayt al-shiʿr, “the line of verse”.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَعِيدِيهِ فَأَعَادَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā aʿīdīhi fa-aʿādathu
sentences.l: And I said to her: Repeat it; and she repeated it.
sentences.i: “Say it to me again,” I said, and she said it again.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَضَيْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَدَخَلْتُ الْمَقْعَدَ فَوَجَدْتُ الصَّبِيَّةَ فِي انْتِظَارِي فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي قَامَتْ وَقَبَّلَتْنِي وَأَجْلَسَتْنِي فِي حِجْرِهَا ثُمَّ أَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا وَقَضَيْنَا أَغْرَاضَنَا كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ
sentences.tr: thumma maḍaytu ilā al-bustāni wa-dakhaltu al-maqʿada fa-wajadtu al-ṣabiyyata fī intiẓārī fa-lammā raʾatnī qāmat wa-qabbalatnī wa-ajlasatnī fī ḥijrihā thumma akalnā wa-sharibnā wa-qaḍaynā aghrāḍanā kamā taqaddama
sentences.l: Then I went to the garden and entered the sitting-place, and I found the young-woman in waiting for me; and when she saw me she rose and kissed me and seated me in her lap. Then we ate and drank and accomplished our purposes, as (has) gone-before.
sentences.i: Then I went to the garden and into the alcove, and found the young woman waiting for me. When she saw me she rose, kissed me and sat me in her lap; then we ate and drank and had our desire of each other, as before.
sentences.n: qaḍaynā aghrāḍanā, “we accomplished our purposes”: the text’s plain phrase for lovemaking. kamā taqaddama, “as went before”: as on the earlier night.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ أَنْشَدْتُهَا الشِّعْرَ وَهُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu anshadtuhā al-shiʿra wa-huwa
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning, I recited to her the verse, and it (is):
sentences.i: When morning came, I recited the verse to her. It goes:

sentences.t: اَلَا اَيُّهَا الْعُشَّاقُ بِاللّٰهِ خَبِّرُوْا * اِذَا اشْتَدَّ عِشْقٌ بِالْفَتَى كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ
sentences.tr: alā ayyuhā al-ʿushshāqu bi-allāhi khabbirū * idhā ishtadda ʿishqun bi-al-fatā kayfa yaṣnaʿu
sentences.l: Ho, O you the lovers, by God, inform: * when a passion grows-severe in the youth, how does he act?
sentences.i: You lovers, tell me, I ask you by God: * when love bears hard upon a young man, what is he to do?
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed. bi-allāhi, “by God”: bi- of the oath. bi-al-fatā: bi- “in, upon”, where the passion takes hold.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْهُ ذَرَفَتْ عَيْنَاهَا بِالدُّمُوعِ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿathu dharafat ʿaynāhā bi-al-dumūʿi wa-anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: And when she heard it, her two eyes shed with the tears, and she recited, saying:
sentences.i: When she heard it her eyes brimmed over with tears, and she answered in verse:

sentences.t: يُدَارِي هَوَاهُ ثُمَّ يَكْتُمُ سِرَّهُ * وَيَصْبِرُ فِي كُلِّ الْاُمُوْرِ وَيَخْضَعُ
sentences.tr: yudārī hawāhu thumma yaktumu sirrahu * wa-yaṣbiru fī kulli al-umūri wa-yakhḍaʿu
sentences.l: He conceals-gently his passion, then hides his secret, * and is patient in all the affairs, and submits.
sentences.i: He keeps his love disguised, and hides his secret, * and bears all things with patience, and submits.
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed. yudārī: to manage something by gentleness and concealment, to keep it from showing.

sentences.t: فَحَفِظْتُهُ وَفَرِحْتُ بِقَضَاءِ حَاجَةِ ابْنَةِ عَمِّي وَخَرَجْتُ وَأَتَيْتُ إِلَى ابْنَةِ عَمِّي فَوَجَدْتُهَا رَاقِدَةً وَأُمِّي عِنْدَ رَأْسِهَا تَبْكِي عَلَى حٰلِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥafiẓtuhu wa-fariḥtu bi-qaḍāʾi ḥājati ibnati ʿammī wa-kharajtu wa-ataytu ilā ibnati ʿammī fa-wajadtuhā rāqidatan wa-ummī ʿinda raʾsihā tabkī ʿalā ḥālihā
sentences.l: And I memorised it, and rejoiced at the accomplishing of the need of the daughter of my uncle; and I went out and came to the daughter of my uncle, and I found her lying-down, and my mother at her head, weeping over her state.
sentences.i: I learned it by heart, glad to have done my cousin’s errand, and I went out and came to my cousin. I found her lying down, and my mother at her head, weeping over her condition.
sentences.n: ḥālihā, “her state”: the print spells حلها without the alif; it is pointed with a dagger alif. fariḥtu bi-, “rejoiced at”: the verb takes bi- for the cause of joy.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهَا قَالَتْ لِي أُمِّي تَبًّا لَكَ مِنِ ابْنِ عَمٍّ كَيْفَ تَتْرُكُ بِنْتَ عَمِّكَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اسْتِوَاءٍ وَلَا تَسْأَلُ عَنْ مَرَضِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu ʿalayhā qālat lī ummī tabban laka min ibni ʿammin kayfa tatruku binta ʿammika ʿalā ghayri istiwāʾin wa-lā tasʾalu ʿan maraḍihā
sentences.l: And when I entered upon her, my mother said to me: Ruin to you, of a cousin! How do you leave the daughter of your uncle upon other-than evenness, and do not ask about her sickness?
sentences.i: When I went in to her, my mother said to me, “Shame on you, what a cousin you are! How can you leave your cousin so unwell, and not even ask after her illness?”
sentences.n: tabban laka, “ruin to you”: a curse, here half a reproach; the print points تبًّا. min ibni ʿammin, “of a cousin”: min of kind after an exclamation, “what a cousin!”. ʿalā ghayri istiwāʾ, “out of evenness”: not in good health.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي ابْنَةُ عَمِّي رَفَعَتْ رَأْسَهَا وَقَعَدَتْ وَقَالَتْ لِي يَا عَزِيزُ هَلْ أَنْشَدْتَهَا الْبَيْتَ الَّذِي أَخْبَرْتُكَ بِهِ قُلْتُ لَهَا نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī ibnatu ʿammī rafaʿat raʾsahā wa-qaʿadat wa-qālat lī yā ʿazīzu hal anshadtahā al-bayta alladhī akhbartuka bihi qultu lahā naʿam
sentences.l: And when the daughter of my uncle saw me, she raised her head and sat-up and said to me: O ʿAzīz, did you recite to her the verse which I told you of? I said to her: Yes.
sentences.i: When my cousin saw me she raised her head and sat up, and said to me, “ʿAzīz, did you recite to her the verse I told you?” “Yes,” I said.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْهُ بَكَتْ وَأَنْشَدَتْنِي بَيْتًا آخَرَ وَحَفِظْتُهُ فَقَالَتْ بِنْتُ عَمِّي أَسْمِعْنِي إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا أَسْمَعْتُهَا إِيَّاهُ بَكَتْ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَأَنْشَدَتْ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿathu bakat wa-anshadatnī baytan ākhara wa-ḥafiẓtuhu fa-qālat bintu ʿammī asmiʿnī iyyāhu fa-lammā asmaʿtuhā iyyāhu bakat bukāʾan shadīdan wa-anshadat hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: “And when she heard it, she wept and recited to me another verse, and I memorised it.” And the daughter of my uncle said: Make me hear it. And when I made her hear it, she wept a severe weeping, and recited these two verses:
sentences.i: “When she heard it she wept, and recited another line to me, and I have it by heart.” “Let me hear it,” said my cousin; and when I had said it to her she wept bitterly and recited these two lines:
sentences.n: asmiʿnī iyyāhu, “make me hear it”: the causative fourth form takes two objects, the second set apart with iyyā-.

sentences.t:
وَكَيْفَ يُدَارِي وَالْهَوَى قَاتِلُ الْفَتَى * وَفِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ قَلْبُهُ يَتَقَطَّعُ
لَقَدْ حَاوَلَ الصَّبْرَ الْجَمِيلَ وَلَمْ يَجِدْ * لَهُ غَيْرَ قَلْبٍ فِي الصَّبَابَةِ يَجْزَعُ
sentences.tr:
wa-kayfa yudārī wa-al-hawā qātilu al-fatā * wa-fī kulli yawmin qalbuhu yataqaṭṭaʿu
laqad ḥāwala al-ṣabra al-jamīla wa-lam yajid * lahu ghayra qalbin fī al-ṣabābati yajzaʿu
sentences.l:
And how shall he conceal-gently, when the passion (is) the slayer of the youth, * and in every day his heart is cut-to-pieces?
He has tried the patience the beautiful, and has not found * for himself other than a heart that in the ardour is-distressed.
sentences.i:
How can he hide it, when love is the young man’s slayer, * and every day his heart is torn to pieces?
He has striven for patience, the fair kind, and found in himself nothing * but a heart that frets in its longing.
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed. It answers the line ʿAzīz has just brought back, taking up its word yudārī. al-ṣabr al-jamīl, “fair patience”: a phrase from the Qurʾān, Jacob’s words on losing Joseph (12:18). ṣabāba: ardent, wasting love.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِي ابْنَةُ عَمِّي إِذَا ذَهَبْتَ إِلَيْهَا عَلَى عَادَتِكَ فَأَنْشِدْهَا هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ الَّذِي سَمِعْتَهُمَا فَقُلْتُ لَهَا سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lī ibnatu ʿammī idhā dhahabta ilayhā ʿalā ʿādatika fa-anshidhā hādhayni al-baytayni alladhī samiʿtahumā fa-qultu lahā samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: Then the daughter of my uncle said to me: When you go to her upon your custom, recite to her these two verses which you have heard. And I said to her: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: Then my cousin said to me, “When you go to her as you are used to, recite to her these two lines you have just heard.” I said to her, “With hearing and obedience.”
sentences.n: alladhī: the print has the singular relative after the dual “two lines”, where Classical Arabic would write alladhayni; a common spoken use. samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan: “hearing and obedience”, the stock formula of assent.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَيْهَا فِى الْبُسْتَانِ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ وَكَانَ بَيْنَنَا مَا كَانَ مِمَّا يَقْصُرُ عَنْ وَصْفِهِ اللِّسَانُ
sentences.tr: thumma dhahabtu ilayhā fī al-bustāni ʿalā al-ʿādati wa-kāna baynanā mā kāna mimmā yaqṣuru ʿan waṣfihi al-lisānu
sentences.l: Then I went to her in the garden upon the custom, and there was between us what there was, of what the tongue falls-short of describing.
sentences.i: Then I went to her in the garden as usual, and there passed between us what passed, more than the tongue can tell.
sentences.n: kāna baynanā mā kāna, “there was between us what there was”: the storyteller’s veil over the lovers’ night.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَرَدْتُ الِانْصِرَافَ أَنْشَدْتُهَا ذَيْنِكَ الْبَيْتَيْنِ إِلَى آخِرِهِمَا فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْهُمَا سَالَتْ مَدَامِعُهَا مِنَ الْمَحَاجِرِ وَأَنْشَدَتْ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aradtu al-inṣirāfa anshadtuhā dhaynika al-baytayni ilā ākhirihimā fa-lammā samiʿathumā sālat madāmiʿuhā mina al-maḥājiri wa-anshadat qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And when I wanted the departing, I recited to her those two verses to their end; and when she heard them, her tears flowed from the eye-sockets, and she recited the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: When I wanted to leave, I recited those two lines to her, to the end; and when she heard them her tears flowed down from her eyes, and she recited the poet’s words:
sentences.n: dhaynika, “those two”: the dual of dhālika. maḥājir: the hollows of the eyes; madāmiʿ, the places the tears run from, so “her tears”.

sentences.t: فَاِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ صَبْرًا لِكِتْمَانِ سِرِّهِ * فَلَيْسَ لَهُ عِنْدِي سِوَى الْمَوْتِ اَنْفَعُ
sentences.tr: fa-in lam yajid ṣabran li-kitmāni sirrihi * fa-laysa lahu ʿindī siwā al-mawti anfaʿu
sentences.l: And if he finds not patience for the hiding of his secret, * then there is not for him, in my view, more-useful other than the death.
sentences.i: And if he cannot find the patience to keep his secret hidden, * then nothing, to my mind, will serve him better than death.
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed. li-kitmāni, “for hiding”: li- of purpose.

sentences.t: فَحَفِظْتُهُ وَتَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ عَلَى ابْنَةِ عَمِّي وَجَدْتُهَا مُلْقَاةً مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا وَأُمِّي جَالِسَةٌ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهَا فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامِي فَتَحَتْ عَيْنَاهَا وَقَالَتْ يَا عَزِيزُ هَلْ أَنْشَدْتَهَا الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥafiẓtuhu wa-tawajjahtu ilā al-bayti fa-lammā dakhaltu ʿalā ibnati ʿammī wajadtuhā mulqātan maghshiyyan ʿalayhā wa-ummī jālisatun ʿinda raʾsihā fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmī fataḥat ʿaynāhā wa-qālat yā ʿazīzu hal anshadtahā al-baytayni
sentences.l: And I memorised it and turned-towards the house; and when I entered upon the daughter of my uncle, I found her thrown-down, fainted upon her, and my mother sitting at her head. And when she heard my speech, she opened her two eyes and said: O ʿAzīz, did you recite to her the two verses?
sentences.i: I learned it by heart and made for home. When I went in to my cousin, I found her lying senseless, in a faint, and my mother sitting at her head. When she heard my voice she opened her eyes and said, “ʿAzīz, did you recite the two lines to her?”
sentences.n: maghshiyyan ʿalayhā, “fainted”: literally “with a covering come over her”, the passive participle with ʿalā. fataḥat ʿaynāhā, “she opened her eyes”: the print has the nominative dual ʿaynāhā where Classical Arabic wants ʿaynayhā as the object; the spoken language uses one form of the dual for both, and it is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ لَهَا نَعَمْ وَلَكِنْ لَمَّا سَمِعَتْهُمَا بَكَتْ وَأَنْشَدَتْنِي هَذَا الْبَيْتَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: qultu lahā naʿam wa-lākin lammā samiʿathumā bakat wa-anshadatnī hādhā al-bayta fa-in lam yajid ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: I said to her: Yes; but when she heard them she wept and recited to me this verse, “And if he finds not”, to its end.
sentences.i: “Yes,” I told her, “but when she heard them she wept, and recited this line to me: ‘And if he cannot find …’” — and so on to the end.
sentences.n: fa-in lam yajid ilā ākhirihi: the text quotes the opening of the line and leaves the rest, “to its end”, to the reader, who has just heard it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْهُ بِنْتُ عَمِّي غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا ثَانِيًا فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ أَنْشَدَتْ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ وَهُمَا هَذَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿathu bintu ʿammī ghushiya ʿalayhā thāniyan fa-lammā afāqat anshadat hādhayni al-baytayni wa-humā hādhāni
sentences.l: And when the daughter of my uncle heard it, it was fainted upon her a second-time; and when she came-to, she recited these two verses, and they (are) these:
sentences.i: When my cousin heard it she fainted a second time, and when she came round she recited these two lines, which are these:
sentences.n: ghushiya ʿalayhā, “she fainted”: an impersonal passive, “a covering came over her”.

sentences.t:
سَمِعْنَا اَطَعْنَا ثُمَّ مُتْنَا فَبَلِّغُوا * سَلَامِي عَلَى مَنْ كَانَ لِلْوَصْلِ يَمْنَعُ
هَنِيْأً لِاَرْبَابِ النَّعِيمِ نَعِيمُهُمْ * وَلِلْعَاشِقِ الْمِسْكِينِ مَا يَتَجَرَّعُ
sentences.tr:
samiʿnā aṭaʿnā thumma mutnā fa-ballighū * salāmī ʿalā man kāna li-al-waṣli yamnaʿu
hanīʾan li-arbābi al-naʿīmi naʿīmuhum * wa-li-al-ʿāshiqi al-miskīni mā yatajarraʿu
sentences.l:
We heard, we obeyed, then we died; so convey * my greeting to whoever was the union withholding.
Wholesome to the lords of the bliss (be) their bliss, * and to the lover, the wretched, what he gulps-down.
sentences.i:
We heard, we obeyed, and then we died: so carry * my greeting to the one who kept our union from us.
Joy to the masters of delight in their delight, * and to the wretched lover, the bitter draught he swallows.
sentences.n: The print points this verse, and it is copied as printed; هَنِيْأً is its spelling of hanīʾan, “may it do (them) good”. li-al-waṣli yamnaʿu: the li- marks the object of the verb, set before it, “who was withholding union”. yatajarraʿu: “gulps down”, used of bitter drink, grief and anger.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ مَضَيْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ عَلَى جَرْيِ عَادَتِي فَوَجَدْتُ الصَّبِيَّةَ فِي انْتِظَارِي فَجَلَسْنَا وَأَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا وَعَمِلْنَا شُغْلَنَا وَنِمْنَا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ فَلَمَّا أَرَدْتُ الِانْصِرَافَ أَنْشَدْتُهَا مَا قَالَتْهُ بِنْتُ عَمِّي
sentences.tr: thumma lammā aqbala al-laylu maḍaytu ilā al-bustāni ʿalā jaryi ʿādatī fa-wajadtu al-ṣabiyyata fī intiẓārī fa-jalasnā wa-akalnā wa-sharibnā wa-ʿamilnā shughlanā wa-nimnā ilā al-ṣabāḥi fa-lammā aradtu al-inṣirāfa anshadtuhā mā qālathu bintu ʿammī
sentences.l: Then when the night came-on, I went to the garden upon the running of my custom, and I found the young-woman in waiting for me; and we sat and ate and drank and did our business and slept until the morning. And when I wanted the departing, I recited to her what the daughter of my uncle had said.
sentences.i: Then, when night came on, I went to the garden as was my habit, and found the young woman waiting for me. We sat, ate and drank, did what we came for, and slept till morning; and when I wanted to leave, I recited to her what my cousin had said.
sentences.n: ʿamilnā shughlanā, “we did our business”: again the plain phrase for lovemaking. ʿalā jaryi ʿādatī: “in the course of my habit”, as usual.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَلِكَ صَرَخَتْ صَرْخَةً عَظِيمَةً وَتَضَجَّرَتْ وَقَالَتْ أَوَّاهْ أَوَّاهْ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ قَائِلَةَ هَذَا الشِّعْرِ قَدْ مَاتَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhālika ṣarakhat ṣarkhatan ʿaẓīmatan wa-taḍajjarat wa-qālat awwāh awwāh wa-allāhi inna qāʾilata hādhā al-shiʿri qad mātat
sentences.l: And when she heard that, she screamed a great scream and was-distressed, and said: Alas, alas! By God, the sayer of this verse has died.
sentences.i: When she heard it she gave a great cry, in anguish, and said, “Alas, alas! By God, the woman who made this verse is dead.”
sentences.n: taḍajjarat: “was vexed, distressed”. awwāh: a cry of grief and pain. qāʾila, “the (woman) who said”: the feminine participle; she has guessed that the lines come from a woman.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ وَيْلَكَ مَا تَقْرُبُ لَكَ قَائِلَةُ هَذَا الشِّعْرِ قُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّهَا ابْنَةُ عَمِّي
sentences.tr: thumma bakat wa-qālat waylaka mā taqrubu laka qāʾilatu hādhā al-shiʿri qultu lahā innahā ibnatu ʿammī
sentences.l: Then she wept and said: Woe to you! What is the sayer of this verse related to you? I said to her: She (is) the daughter of my uncle.
sentences.i: Then she wept and said, “Woe to you! What is she to you, the woman who made this verse?” I told her, “She is my cousin.”
sentences.n: mā taqrubu laka, “how is she related to you”: qaruba li-, “be near to, be kin to”, in a spoken use.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ كَذَبْتَ وَاللَّهِ لَوْ كَانَتِ ابْنَةَ عَمِّكَ لَكَانَ عِنْدَكَ لَهَا مِنَ الْمَحَبَّةِ مِثْلُ مَا عِنْدَهَا لَكَ فَأَنْتَ الَّذِي قَتَلْتَهَا قَتَلَكَ اللَّهُ كَمَا قَتَلْتَهَا وَاللَّهِ لَوْ أَخْبَرْتَنِي أَنَّ لَكَ ابْنَةَ عَمٍّ مَا كُنْتُ قَرَّبْتُكَ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: qālat kadhabta wa-allāhi law kānati ibnata ʿammika la-kāna ʿindaka lahā mina al-maḥabbati mithlu mā ʿindahā laka fa-anta alladhī qataltahā qatalaka allāhu kamā qataltahā wa-allāhi law akhbartanī anna laka ibnata ʿammin mā kuntu qarrabtuka minnī
sentences.l: She said: You have lied! By God, if she were the daughter of your uncle, there would be with you for her, of the love, the like of what is with her for you. So you (are) the one who killed her — may God kill you as you killed her! By God, if you had told me that you have a daughter of an uncle, I would not have brought you near me.
sentences.i: She said, “You lie! By God, if she were your cousin you would have as much love for her as she has for you. You are the one who killed her — God kill you as you killed her! By God, if you had told me you had a cousin, I would never have let you near me.”
sentences.n: la-kāna: the la- that opens the answer to a law, “if”.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ تُفَسِّرُ لِي تِلْكَ الْإِشَارَاتِ الَّتِي كُنْتِ تُشِيرِينَ بِهَا إِلَيَّ وَهِيَ الَّتِي عَلَّمَتْنِي كَيْفَ أَصِلُ إِلَيْكِ وَأَفْعَلُ مَعَكِ وَلَوْلَا هِيَ مَا وَصَلْتُ إِلَيْكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā innahā kānat tufassiru lī tilka al-ishārāti allatī kunti tushīrīna bihā ilayya wa-hiya allatī ʿallamatnī kayfa aṣilu ilayki wa-afʿalu maʿaki wa-lawlā hiya mā waṣaltu ilayki
sentences.l: And I said to her: She used to interpret for me those signs which you used to sign with to me, and she (is) the one who taught me how I should reach you and do with you; and were it not for her, I would not have reached you.
sentences.i: I said to her, “It was she who explained to me the signs you used to make to me; she taught me how to reach you and how to behave with you, and but for her I would never have reached you.”
sentences.n: ashāra bi-, “sign with”: bi- names what the sign is made with. lawlā hiya, “were it not for her”: lawlā takes the independent pronoun, as in Classical usage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَهَلْ عَرَفَتْ بِنَا قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَتْ حَسَّرَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَى شَبَابِكَ كَمَا حَسَّرْتَهَا عَلَى شَبَابِهَا ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِي رُحِ انْظُرْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-hal ʿarafat binā qultu naʿam qālat ḥassaraka allāhu ʿalā shabābika kamā ḥassartahā ʿalā shabābihā thumma qālat lī ruḥi unẓurhā
sentences.l: And she said: And did she know about us? I said: Yes. She said: May God make-you-grieve over your youth, as you made-her-grieve over her youth. Then she said to me: Go, look-at her.
sentences.i: “And did she know about us?” she asked. “Yes,” I said. She said, “May God make you mourn your youth as you made her mourn hers!” Then she said to me, “Go and see her.”
sentences.n: ʿarafa bi-, “know about, learn of”: the verb takes bi- here, a spoken use. ḥassaraka allāhu ʿalā shabābika: may God make you lament your youth, that is, cut it short. ruḥ: the spoken imperative of rāḥa, “go”.

sentences.t: فَذَهَبْتُ وَخَاطِرِي مُتَشَوِّشٌ وَمَا زِلْتُ مَاشِيًا إِلَى أَنْ أَتَيْتُ إِلَى زُقَاقِنَا فَسَمِعْتُ عِيَاطًا فَسَأَلْتُ عَنْهُ فَقِيلَ لِي إِنَّ عَزِيزَةَ وَجَدْنَاهَا خَلْفَ الْبَابِ مَيِّتَةً
sentences.tr: fa-dhahabtu wa-khāṭirī mutashawwishun wa-mā ziltu māshiyan ilā an ataytu ilā zuqāqinā fa-samiʿtu ʿiyāṭan fa-saʾaltu ʿanhu fa-qīla lī inna ʿazīzata wajadnāhā khalfa al-bābi mayyitatan
sentences.l: And I went, and my mind troubled, and I did not cease walking until I came to our lane; and I heard wailing, and I asked about it, and it was said to me: ʿAzīza — we found her behind the door, dead.
sentences.i: I went, my mind in turmoil, and walked on until I came to our lane. There I heard wailing, and when I asked about it I was told, “ʿAzīza — we found her behind the door, dead.”
sentences.n: mutashawwish, “troubled, confused”, and ʿiyāṭ, “wailing, crying out”: spoken words. inna ʿazīzata wajadnāhā: the name is put first and taken up again by the pronoun, as people speak.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلْتُ الدَّارَ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي أُمِّي قَالَتْ إِنَّ خَطِيئَتَهَا فِي ذِمَّتِكَ وَعُنُقِكَ فَلَا سَامَحَكَ اللَّهُ مِنْ دَمِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma dakhaltu al-dāra fa-lammā raʾatnī ummī qālat inna khaṭīʾatahā fī dhimmatika wa-ʿunuqika fa-lā sāmaḥaka allāhu min damihā
sentences.l: Then I entered the house, and when my mother saw me she said: The sin of her (is) in your charge and (on) your neck; so may God not pardon you of her blood!
sentences.i: Then I went into the house, and when my mother saw me she said, “The guilt of her death is on your conscience and on your neck; may God never forgive you her blood!”
sentences.n: fī dhimmatika wa-ʿunuqika, “in your charge and on your neck”: the guilt is his to answer for. sāmaḥa min, “forgive (someone) for”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
